The second is the small transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*) of two zhang and six chi, which responds to the capacities of those of the Two Vehicles (*śrāvaka* and *pratyekabuddha*) as well as ordinary worldlings (*pṛthagjana*), preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles (*triyāna*).
The third is the transformation body that appears according to the species; this refers to appearing as a monkey among monkeys, as a deer among deer, and so forth.
These—the other recompense body (*saṃbhogakāya*) and the three types of transformation bodies—all take the transformed, untainted (*anāsrava*) five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*) as their essence.
Second, based on the three bodies as explained within the *dharmatā*, they are established according to the three aspects of essence (*svabhāva*), characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*), and function (*vṛtti*).

The *Awakening of Faith* states: "The first is the greatness of essence (*svabhāva-mahattva*); it refers to the fact that all phenomena are the equality of *tathatā*, for there is neither increase nor decrease. The commentary says:
The essence-body (*svabhāvakāya*) and its characteristics are the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*). Second is the greatness of characteristics (*lakṣaṇamahātmya*), which refers to the Tathāgatagarbha;

for it is fully endowed with immeasurable inherent qualities of nature. The commentary states: Based on the non-empty treasury, the qualities of nature are inherently complete; through cultivation, one emerges from obstructions.

That which corresponds to this is called the true recompense body (*sambhogakāya*). Third is the Great Function (*mahopāya*), because it is able to produce the causes and effects of mundane and supramundane goodness.

The commentary states: This refers to the Buddha’s natural great function of illusory manifestation, which accords with those on the stages prior to the grounds (*bhūmi*) as well as ordinary beings, causing them to initially accomplish mundane goodness;
this is called the transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*) (termed "mundane goodness"). If it is the other, the recompense body...

According to the capacities of those who have ascended the stages (*bhūmi*), the Mahāyāna Dharma is taught, causing them ultimately to achieve supramundane goodness (the realization of truth on the stages is termed "supramundane goodness").

What this treatise refers to as the *dharmakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* means that the qualities of nature (*xingde*) are conjoined with the essence of nature (*xingti*), such that principle and wisdom are non-dual.
The Dharma-body and the Reward-body share a single source. Thus, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* states: "Only suchness and the wisdom of suchness remain.
This also constitutes the meaning of the two bodies (*dvikāya*). According to the teachings of the Huayan school, Vairocana Buddha possesses two kinds of ten bodies (*daśakāya*).
The first is categorized by merging the three periods of time and expanding them into ten bodies: (1) the body of sentient beings, (2) the body of the land, (3) the... [text truncated]
1. The body of karmic retribution; 2. the body of a śrāvaka; 3. the body of a pratyekabuddha; 4. the body of a bodhisattva; 5. the body of a Tathāgata; 6. the body of wisdom;
7. the dharma-body; 8. the space-body. Second, regarding the Buddha-body itself, it inherently possesses these ten bodies.

1. The body of enlightenment (*bodhi-kāya*). 2. The body of vows (*praṇidhāna-kāya*). 3. The transformation body (*nirmāṇa-kāya*). 4. The body of sustaining power (*baladhāraṇa-kāya*). 5. The body adorned with the primary and secondary marks (*lakṣaṇānuvyañjana-vyūha-kāya*).
6. The body of majestic power (*anubhāva-kāya*). 7. The mind-made body (*manomaya-kāya*). 8. The body of merit (*puṇya-kāya*). 9. The Dharma body (*dharma-kāya*). 10. The wisdom body (*jñāna-kāya*).

Regarding these two types of ten bodies, if they are subsumed within the three bodies (*trikāya*), it is as follows: among the aforementioned ten bodies, the *dharmakāya* and the *ākāśakāya* correspond to the *dharmakāya* among the three bodies;
the *tathāgatakāya* and the *jñānakāya* correspond to the *saṃbhogakāya*; and the remaining six bodies are subsumed within both the *dharmakāya* and the *nirmāṇakāya*.
This is because [the former] is the essence of the *dharmakāya*, while [the latter] manifests lands and so forth in accordance with sentient beings. Second, in terms of...

Regarding the ten bodies within the internal [classification]: the Dharma-body is entirely identical [to the aforementioned]. The five bodies—vow, transformation, power-sustenance, and mind-born—are identical to the Transformation-body (nirmāṇakāya).

The three bodies consisting of marks and signs, majestic power, and merit and virtue communicate with both the Universal and Transformation-bodies. The wisdom-penetration communicates with all three bodies.

The specific [teachings] pertain only to the Dharma-body and the Reward-body. What is elucidated in this present treatise, however, encompasses both the Dharma-nature school and the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao).
By taking the fundamental to govern the derivative, it also subsumes all other schools.
